title: observability: token-level KV cost/latency breakdowns + dashboard & alert tuning
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Context: We need better visibility into per-token costs and latency for KV-backed responses delivered by the serving runtime. Current dashboards surface aggregate token cost but mix KV cacheable vs non-cacheable traffic, which makes it hard to tune batching/eviction policies and alert thresholds. This PR introduces token-level KV cache metrics, a curated Grafana dashboard, and revised alert rules to reduce noise while ensuring high-impact regressions are caught.

Summary of changes: added new metric labels (kv_hit, kv_miss, kv_evicted) and per-token cost breakdowns, enhanced tracing spans to propagate kv_* tags, new Grafana dashboard with panels for cost/latency by token class, updated alert rules with severity tiers and dynamic thresholds, and docs for interpreting the dashboard.

What I changed (high level):
- services/kv: emit token-level metrics and tags (kv_hit/kv_miss/kv_evicted, token_length_bucket, model_variant)
- telemetry: serializer updates to ensure metric tags are stable and low-cardinality
- dashboards: new token_kv_cost_latency.json (Grafana JSON) with overview + drilldowns
- alerts: token_kv_latency.rules with INFO/WARN/CRITICAL tiers and cooldowns to reduce flapping
- docs: docs/observability/token-level-dashboard.md with interpretation guide and runbook snippets
- tests: unit tests for metrics collector and a small integration test that validates metric emission under simulated workload

Checklist: [x] metric names and tags reviewed with telemetry team; [x] dashboard usability reviewed with SRE; [x] alerts tuned via 48h preprod run; [x] documented runbook snippets for pagers; [x] added unit + integration tests.

Why this is safe: metric changes are additive (new metrics and tags); existing metrics remain unchanged. Alerting changes lower noisy signals (INFO tier) and only escalate on sustained degradations.\n
Notes: The Grafana dashboard references recording rules that will be added in a follow-up (ENG-7410) to reduce query load — those are out-of-band to keep this PR reviewable.

Migration/rollout: rollout is safe to merge to main; dashboard will be published to the observability stack on merge. SRE will monitor for 72h and we have a rollback plan (revert alert rule changes) in case of unexpected noise.

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Left a few nits on the metric names — prefer kv_hit_count -> kv_hit_total to follow our prometheus conventions. Also suggest adding model_variant as a label only for high-sample models to avoid cardinality spikes.
Aisha Patel: Addressed in telemetry/serializers change, added sampling guard for model_variant (see metrics_tags.go). Resolved Diego's nit and added unit test.
Sophie Liang: Alert thresholds look good after 48h preprod run. Can we add a suppressor for maintenance windows?
Aisha Patel: Added maintenance window annotation support to alert rules; updated docs with example kubernetes-maintenance label. Marking Sophie as resolved.
Ethan Ross: Approved after verifying dashboard panels render in staging and CI passed. Recommendation to add a short runbook snippet into the docs; author included it.
CI: nightly/integration: tests passed (re-ran flaky test once)
release_notes: Added token-level KV cache cost & latency dashboard; introduced token-level KV metrics and tags; tuned multi-tier alerts (INFO/WARN/CRITICAL) to reduce noise; updated observability docs and runbook.
